scope: Documentation Site UX Optimization: Viewport-Scoped ScrollTrigger Disable, Arrow Navigation Controls, Contained Card/Folder Window Scrolling, and Slide Filmstrip Up/Down Transitions

tasks.title: Disable GSAP ScrollTrigger on Mobile and Tablet Viewports
tasks.description: Conditionally disable or kill GSAP ScrollTrigger pin/scrub animations on mobile and tablet screen widths (window.innerWidth < 1024px or via gsap.matchMedia). On mobile and tablet devices, fall back to native smooth touch scrolling so users are not trapped by desktop horizontal pin scrubbers, ensuring that card contents and documentation text scroll naturally without scroll jank.

tasks.title: Add Accessible Navigation Arrow Controls for Slides and Folders
tasks.description: Implement floating/docked directional navigation arrow controls (<button aria-label='Previous'> and <button aria-label='Next'>) on both the Home Page folder flow and the Documentation slide deck presentation views. The buttons must allow direct previous/next jumping across slides and folder sections, remain accessible across mobile, tablet, and desktop, dynamically disable when at bounds (index 0 or last index), and synchronize active thumbnail/progress indicators.

tasks.title: Isolate Internal Card/Folder Window Scroll from Main Component Container
tasks.description: Ensure that vertical scrolling inside an active slide card or home folder panel is completely isolated and strictly contained within its dedicated inner window frame. Apply `overscroll-behavior: contain` and CSS containment (`isolate`, `overflow-y-auto`, hiding outer document scrollbars or setting parent viewport overflow to hidden) so internal content scrolling does not bubble up, cause window bounce, or show visible parent page scrollbars on the main component canvas.

tasks.title: Implement Slide-Up & Slide-Down Show/Hide Animations for Mobile Slide Filmstrip
tasks.description: Upgrade the collapsible mobile/tablet slide filmstrip with smooth slide-up and slide-down transition animations using GSAP or CSS hardware-accelerated transitions (transform: translateY(0) to translateY(100%)). When expanding, the filmstrip smoothly slides up from the bottom; when collapsing, it smoothly slides down into the minimized handle/bar without jarring pop-in or layout thrashing.
